meta.method: Searched public news and official sources for literacy and education news on the Caribbean. Summaries are written by the Observatory in its own words; headlines link to the original publisher.
meta.disclaimer: Inclusion is not endorsement. Figures quoted in news items are reported by those sources and have not been verified by the Observatory; they do not enter the statistics dashboard until audited.

points: Secondary literacy is in focus in Jamaica: a mid-November letter in the Jamaica Observer cites the Ministry's reading of the 2026 Primary Exit Profile, that about 8,700 students entered high school below proficiency in language arts.

Teacher capacity remains the main lever across the region — from reading-methods training in Jamaica to Barbados's structured literacy programme, which the Ministry links to reading gains in a sample of primary students.
Regional assessment is expanding: CXC has new literacy and numeracy standards, Guyana is adding Grade 2 and Grade 4 literacy assessments, and the OECS runs annual Grade 2 reading assessments.
Data watch: the World Bank's literacy series were last updated on 11 November 2026; the dashboard reflects that release.

items.title: There is a literacy crisis in high schools
items.summary: Letter to the editor arguing that high schools face a literacy crisis, citing the Ministry's conclusion from 2026 PEP results that roughly 8,700 incoming students were below proficient in language arts.

items.title: Teachers at the Forefront of Digital Transformation
items.summary: Press release on teachers at Elletson Primary building confidence to use digital technology in everyday teaching.

items.title: A brief history of literacy in Jamaica
items.summary: Feature tracing Jamaica's literacy efforts from early free schools through adult literacy work in the 1960s to the JAMAL programme of the 1970s.

items.title: WWKIDS Conference trains teachers in proven reading methods
items.summary: Report on a conference training Jamaican teachers in reading instruction methods.

items.title: Reading renaissance — results continue to give implementers of grade-seven literacy initiative reason to smile
items.summary: Report on continued positive results from a grade-seven literacy initiative in Jamaica.

items.title: Stronger literacy push after exam decline
items.summary: Barbados steps up literacy support for students following a decline in examination results.

items.title: British Virgin Islands tops OECS in Grade 2 reading and mathematics assessments
items.summary: Government release on the annual OECS Grade 2 reading and mathematics assessments, in which the Virgin Islands ranked first among eight participating states. The assessments are a possible public source for the Observatory's foundational-literacy audit.

items.title: 79 per cent of PEP students master literacy, 75 per cent numeracy
items.summary: Report that 79% of students leaving primary school in June 2026 demonstrated literacy mastery and 75% numeracy mastery. National assessment results like these are queued for the Observatory's audit.

items.title: Reading levels improve by over 40 per cent in two years
items.summary: Barbados's Chief Education Officer reports reading gains among a sample of primary students under the National Literacy Programme, supported by structured-literacy training for over 587 teachers and a daily 35-minute reading period.

items.title: CXC develops new literacy and numeracy standards aimed at improving performance in key subjects
items.summary: The Caribbean Examinations Council has developed new literacy and numeracy standards to lift outcomes in English and mathematics across the region.

items.title: Guyana Moves to Boost Literacy With New School Assessments
items.summary: Guyana plans literacy assessments at Grade Two and Grade Four amid regional concern about reading outcomes. Publication date not shown on the page retrieved.

items.title: LITERACY: AI-Powered Reading Support for Classrooms
items.summary: Research spotlight on an AI-driven tutoring system designed to support reading in large, under-resourced classrooms. Date not shown on the page retrieved.
